Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a diffuse bilateral reticulonodular pattern involving all lung zones, and the blunting of the costophrenic angles (particularly on the left) indicates the presence of pleural effusion. This combination of widespread interstitial markings and fluid is most consistent with an interstitial lung disease process among the provided choices, whereas options suggesting upper lobe predominance (LCH), absence of pattern (pneumonia), or isolated middle zone findings (sarcoidosis) do not match the imaging.
